introduction: On this Sunday, Zephaniah tells the humble of the land to seek the Lord. In the Gospel, Jesus goes up the mountain and proclaims the Beatitudes: blessed are the poor in spirit, the meek, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers. Paul reminds us that God chose the weak and lowly of the world. Let us take the Beatitudes as our way of life.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven. Let us bring our prayers to the Lord.
intentions: For the Church: that she may live the Beatitudes and be a home for the poor in spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who mourn: that they may be comforted. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peacemakers in places of conflict: that they may be called children of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those persecuted for the sake of righteousness: that they may rejoice in their reward in heaven. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may become meek, merciful and pure in heart. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you have chosen the weak and lowly of the world to share your Kingdom. Give us the spirit of the Beatitudes, and make us blessed in your sight. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Blessed
reflection.body:
The prophet Zephaniah speaks to "all you humble of the land" and tells them, "Seek the LORD... Seek righteousness. Seek humility." God will leave "an afflicted and poor people," who will "take refuge in the LORD's name." God's future belongs to the humble.

In the Gospel, Jesus goes up a mountain, sits down like a teacher, and begins the Sermon on the Mount. Matthew wants us to think of Moses receiving the Law on Mount Sinai. Jesus is giving the new law of the Kingdom, and it begins with blessing.

"Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven. Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted. Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth." Jesus goes on: blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, the merciful, the pure in heart, the peacemakers, and those persecuted for righteousness' sake.

These words turn the world's values upside down. The world blesses the rich, the strong and the successful. Jesus blesses the humble, the grieving, the gentle and the merciful. The Beatitudes are also a portrait of Jesus himself: he is the meek one, the merciful one, the peacemaker, the one persecuted for righteousness.

Paul tells the Corinthians to look at themselves: "not many are wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, and not many noble." Instead, "God chose the weak things of the world." No one can boast before God, so "He who boasts, let him boast in the Lord."

The Beatitudes are not a list of impossible ideals but a path, and Jesus walks it with us. This week, choose one Beatitude and try to live it each day. And pray for someone who is mourning, or for a peacemaker in a troubled place.
